requirements.title: Qualify a deterministic count and its native-time correlation for every path
requirements.spec: THE SYSTEM SHALL implement exactly the 41 census cases below through the actual owned code. Each case has warm/cold, normal/checkpoint/recovery, fresh/replay and held/released-reader branches where the census names them. Its count vector includes instructions only on a qualified reproducible runner; otherwise named calls, actual indexed/row visits, copied/encoded bytes, lock acquisitions and scopes, queue high-water, RPC/syscall counts, appends and physical fsync/fdatasync/full-flush calls are used. A BTree lookup is logarithmic: one API probe does not mean flat instruction cost. Feature-gated counters are off in every normal release and add no production lock or allocation; no new ordinary public interface or dependency is inferred. Count the actual cross-crate request once, retain child/stage attribution, and never double-add nested rows. Seed fixtures outside the region, but include every real reopen, rebuild, retry and durable commit the operation itself performs. Bench workload/digest/counter version, synthetic identity/input bytes, pinned toolchain/profile/OS/allocator and exact completion event are stored with the result. Census source formulas are BEFORE evidence, not measured instruction baselines. Missing numeric baseline/correlation remains unqualified, never 0. Ratchet admission requires repeated identical counts and paired native same-workload increased/reduced-work runs proving the selected metric tracks relevant caller, durable-completion or backlog time. No quiet-machine hold, timer wait or trace-overhead-as-native proof. Ratchets only decrease; changed fixtures, reduced populations or raised limits fail. Never down and never break are checked alongside the count: retain existing stream/authority/durable acknowledgement and all old assertions. N comes from the authenticated unique roster; fixed 1/25/75 diagnostic fixtures remain explicit inputs, not invented live census. Report equal-work N/3N plus independent H/R/Q/J/Nnonce/T/M dimensions.

requirements.title: Capture and persistence: independently bounded count/fix slices
requirements.spec: THE SYSTEM SHALL execute the following named path slices without changing their visible outputs, authority, ordering or acknowledgement boundary. A slice is one 30-minute WRITE box for one named cost and its runnable red/green/count fixture, followed by a separate 30-minute qualification box after its whole agreed change is written. A row naming a/b costs is split into separate a and b boxes; those are not permission to run a partial assembled gate. The first write box for each row adds its exact case/counters and records the unrun source formula; the next owned fix box implements only the named reduction. The lead issues exact code ownership/check conditions before any implementation. At a ceiling, hand back the exact written/checked state and next bounded act; never claim a complex migration finished merely because a box elapsed. Already bounded zero-work paths get regression guards, not fictitious below-zero improvements. A growing or redundant cost must strictly beat its named BEFORE formula at equal true output/input, and all other branch counts may not regress. Necessary payload, actual recipients, returned rows, policy depth and durable minimums remain explicit dimensions. Each slice carries never down via AGENTS-004 survival/custody, never slow via R1 count+correlation+ratchet, never break via observed behavioural red/green and signals, and scales via equal-work N/3N/unrelated-history tests. No Table/map/policy guard may span disk, network, broker or pipe waits; no whole-state clone or global historical scan is hidden in a helper. Stored-shape/index changes use the actual installed-shape migration owner, preserving every still-live id and retry window; index recovery is tested from old bytes. Necessary storage B3 backend seams remain prerequisites, not assumptions or alternate durability policy. DIRECTORY-064 delivery and qualification requirements are referenced, never specified a second time.

requirements.title: Feed and budget enforcement: independently bounded count/fix slices
requirements.spec: THE SYSTEM SHALL execute the following named path slices without changing their visible outputs, authority, ordering or acknowledgement boundary. A slice is one 30-minute WRITE box for one named cost and its runnable red/green/count fixture, followed by a separate 30-minute qualification box after its whole agreed change is written. A row naming a/b costs is split into separate a and b boxes; those are not permission to run a partial assembled gate. The first write box for each row adds its exact case/counters and records the unrun source formula; the next owned fix box implements only the named reduction. The lead issues exact code ownership/check conditions before any implementation. At a ceiling, hand back the exact written/checked state and next bounded act; never claim a complex migration finished merely because a box elapsed. Already bounded zero-work paths get regression guards, not fictitious below-zero improvements. A growing or redundant cost must strictly beat its named BEFORE formula at equal true output/input, and all other branch counts may not regress. Necessary payload, actual recipients, returned rows, policy depth and durable minimums remain explicit dimensions. Each slice carries never down via AGENTS-004 survival/custody, never slow via R1 count+correlation+ratchet, never break via observed behavioural red/green and signals, and scales via equal-work N/3N/unrelated-history tests. No Table/map/policy guard may span disk, network, broker or pipe waits; no whole-state clone or global historical scan is hidden in a helper. Stored-shape/index changes use the actual installed-shape migration owner, preserving every still-live id and retry window; index recovery is tested from old bytes. Necessary storage B3 backend seams remain prerequisites, not assumptions or alternate durability policy. DIRECTORY-064 delivery and qualification requirements are referenced, never specified a second time.
